item.title: Happiness is just a distraction
item.description:
I’ve recently come to the conclusion that life is, by default, taking us toward destruction. A great piece of evidence for this is death—everyone dies in the end. There are many similar examples around us: plants die, our electronic devices eventually stop working like they once did, food goes bad and starts to smell, and we become physically less capable as we age.

All we do in life is ignore this fact and try to delay the destruction we’re all headed for. These efforts are what keep us sane—what we call happiness. Yet, happiness isn’t some ultimate state; it’s merely our way of escaping the fact that, in the end, it’s all about destruction.

item.title: Using a Linux Laptop as a Hotspot for a PS5
item.description:
It was Thanksgiving week, and with Black Friday happening, I finally decided to get a PS5. I didn’t expect it to feel like such a big moment, but walking out of Best Buy with the box in hand was surprisingly exciting—almost like driving off with a new car. I even buckled it into the passenger seat on the way home.

Once I got back, though, I ran into a small issue. To connect the PS5 to the university Wi-Fi, I needed to register its MAC address on iprequest.stanford.edu. Unfortunately, the site was down at the time. Since my laptop was already registered and had internet access, I found a workaround: I set up a Wi-Fi hotspot on my laptop and shared the connection with the PS5. It worked smoothly, and I was able to get everything up and running without much delay.

item.title: First Post
item.description:
I am in love with this new extremely minimal theme designed by Yihui. It also supports LaTeX math expressions. Here is the induction axiom for structural induction on type $\tau$, that I just copied from our current draft on Overleaf:

$$ \biggl( \bigwedge_{c \in \Sigma_{\tau}} \Bigl[ \forall_{i = 1}^{n_c} y_{c,i} . \forall_{k \in P_c} w_{c,k} . \exists u_c . \bigl( (\bigwedge_{j \in P_c} L[y_{c,j}, w_{c,j}]) \rightarrow L[c(\bar{y_c}), u_c] \bigr) \Bigr] \biggr) \rightarrow \forall z .\exists x. L[z, x] $$
